data.name: Hud
data.gender_notes: Hud is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Hud is a prophet in Islamic tradition, often associated with guidance and protection. The name Hud carries the meaning “Guide or Prophet” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Hud usually hope their child will grow to embody guide or prophet and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: In Surah Hud, Allah SWT says, 'And to (the tribe of) 'Ad (We sent) their brother Hud. He said, 'O my people, worship Allah! You have no deity other than Him. You are only inventing (lies).'
data.etymology: Hud belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Guide or Prophet.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hud total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_arabic.name: ھود
in_arabic.meaning: نبي الله الذي أرسل إلى قوم عاد
in_arabic.long_meaning: ھو نبي الله ورسوله الذي أرسل إلى قوم عاد لدعوتهم إلى الله وإلى توحيد الله عز وجل، وھو أحد الأنبياء المذكورين في القرآن الكريم، وقد ورد ذكره في سورة ھود

in_urdu.name: ہود
in_urdu.meaning: اللہ کا نبی جو قوم عاد کے لئے بھیجا گیا تھا
in_urdu.long_meaning: ہود علیہ السلام اللہ کا نبی تھے جنہیں قوم عاد کے لئے رسول کے طور پر بھیجا گیا تھا۔ ان کا ذکر قرآن کریم میں ھود سورة میں کیا گیا ہے۔ وہ عاد قوم کو اللہ کی طرف دعوت دینے اور توحید الٰہی پر زور دینے کے لئے آئے تھے

in_hindi.name: हूद
in_hindi.meaning: भगवान का नबी जो क़ौम आद के लिए भेजा गया था
in_hindi.long_meaning: हूद अलैहिस्सलाम भगवान के नबी थे जिन्हें क़ौम आद के लिए रसूल के रूप में भेजा गया था। उनका उल्लेख क़ुरआन-ए-करीम में सूरत हूद में किया गया है। वह आद क़ौम को अल्लाह की ओर دعوت देने और तौहीद अल्लाह पर ज़ोर देने के लिए आए थे

in_english.name: Hud
in_english.meaning: Prophet of Allah sent to Ad people
in_english.long_meaning: Hud is a prophet in Islam, sent by Allah to the Ad people to call them to monotheism. He is mentioned in the Quran, specifically in Surah Hud. The name Hud is derived from the Arabic root 'H-W-D', which means 'to guide' or 'to lead'. His story serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and submission to God's will

data.cultural_impact: The name Hud is associated with one of the prophets revered in Islamic teachings. In Arabic, the name Hud means "far-off" or "distant." This metaphorical name represents Hud's role as a prophet of guidance, particularly for the Ad community in pre-Islamic Arabia, who were known for their wayward behavior and disregard for faith. The name Hud serves as a reminder of the importance of seeking guidance and staying firmly on the righteous path, especially during periods of spiritual uncertainty and moral decay.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic tradition, the name Hud holds deep spiritual significance as a symbol of divine protection and guidance. It emphasizes that even in the darkest of times, when one may feel distant or lost, Allah (God) sends messengers and prophets like Hud to guide humanity back to the path of righteousness and virtuous living. The name Hud is a powerful reminder of the presence and power of God, inspiring faith, devotion, and a strong sense of purpose and direction in life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Guide or Prophet" symbolizes Hud is a prophet in Islamic tradition, often associated with guidance and protection.. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Hud serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of guide or prophet.

historical_references.context: Islamic prophet and messenger of Allah, Hud was a prophet sent to the people of Ad. He warned them of the impending punishment of Allah for their disobedience and idolatry. The people of Ad rejected Hud's message and mocked him. Allah then sent a flood to destroy them.
